issues.issue: Whether the best interests of the child (BIOC) assessment of Sam was reasonable
issues.applicant_position: BIOC assessment ignored Sam's psychological harm, school evidence, father's abuse and his views.
issues.respondent_position: Officer considered Sam's best interests and gave positive weight; a positive BIOC does not decide the H&C result.
issues.result_text: BIOC analysis had serious shortcomings, so the BIOC finding and the overall decision are unreasonable.

issues.issue: Whether the officer reasonably assessed the applicants' establishment, including an 'exceptional' standard
issues.applicant_position: Officer set an impossible 'exceptional establishment' threshold and compared establishment unfairly to others.
issues.respondent_position: Officer reasonably compared establishment with similar individuals; Sam's establishment was considered in the BIOC analysis.
issues.result_text: Requiring an explanation of exceptional establishment would impose undue rigidity; officer's establishment assessment was reasonable.

issues.issue: Whether the officer's findings on mental health, hardship and country conditions were reasonable
issues.applicant_position: Officer ignored psychotherapist evidence and made speculative findings about support, jobs and recourse in China.
issues.respondent_position: Officer reasonably assessed mental health evidence; availability of treatment in China was a relevant consideration.
issues.result_text: Some findings were reasonable and supported, but others were speculative and unsupported by evidence.
